newsitem.title: CHINA: Cathay cargo total rises again in May.
newsitem.headline: Cathay cargo total rises again in May.

text.p: The amount of cargo carried by Cathay Pacific Airways Limited continued to rise during May despite the grounding of its Airbus fleet because of engine gearbox problems for part of the month. Airline statistics show 14.5 percent more cargo was carried during the month compared to the same month last year.
The rise is in line with a bouyant trend in cargo carried by the Hong Kong airline which has reported double digit cargo growth every month so far this year.

Cathay also reported a 19.1 per cent increase in the payload indicator Freight Tonne Kilometres (FTKs) along with a 5.8 per cent increase in Freight Available Tonne Kilometres (FATKs). Available Tonne Kilometres, which is the sum of the products obtained bv multiplying the number of tonnes of capacity available for passenger and freight carrying revenue load on each flight stage by the flight stage distance, also increased by 7.3 per cent.

Cargo load factor increased by 7.8 per cent month on month to 69.2 per cent. Passenger load factor also increased by 1.2 per cent along with a 0.3 per cent rise in the number of passengers carried and a 1.8 increase in the number of flights during the month to 1,804.
